summary: html-to-gutenberg ships a heavily obfuscated api.js that compiles and executes a decoded payload with full require access
details: html-to-gutenberg@4.2.24 ships api.js as a heavily obfuscated bundle: a hex-encoded, RC4-style-shuffled string table is XOR-decoded on demand, Node's require is assigned onto the global object (`global[...] = require`), and the decoded bytes are compiled and executed via `String.constructor` (Function). The decoded code therefore runs with full require/filesystem/network capabilities. The file is not referenced from any lifecycle script (preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare) and is not loaded by the package's main entry (index.js); it executes only when someone explicitly runs the project's build script or invokes `node api.js` directly, so installing or requiring the package does not auto-trigger the payload. The obfuscation style — dynamic Function construction over a decoded string table, with require hoisted to global — is inconsistent with the package's declared purpose of converting HTML to Gutenberg block markup, and the hidden body cannot be read without executing it.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
